title: Regional arbitrator: p50/p95 latency-delta + composite network-penalty for tiered fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We need an arbitrator service that decides region preference in real time by combining p50 and p95 latency signals with a compact network-health penalty. The goal is to reduce user-visible tail latency and avoid oscillation during short-lived spikes while preserving cost tiering (hosted -> dedicated -> private) and model-variant fallbacks. Current region selector uses an oversimplified composite score that under-reacts to p95 spikes and over-reacts to transient p50 variance, causing tail-slow requests and unnecessary cross-region traffic.
background: Incidents over the last quarter showed cases where p95 increased in a single POP because of transient upstream flaps; the selector kept sending traffic there due to good p50, leading to increased user retries and SLO breaches. See postmortem: https://confluence.redwood.ai/incident/IR-2026-01-pop-p95-spike. Existing tickets: ENG-6234 (telemetry-driven region routing network health score) and ENG-46288 (latency-slo-shepherding region routing) explored ingredients but left open how to fuse deltas and hysteresis with tier and variant constraints.
acceptance_criteria: New arbitrator decisions logged and exposed in /internal/routing/decisions with per-request reasoning (p50,p95,net_penalty,final_score)
P95-sensitive weight increases decision to demote a region when p95 delta exceeds threshold for >= 2 minutes
Avoid flip-flop: region change lockout of 60s after a promoted/demoted decision unless sustained degradation persists
Respect cost tiers: do not route to higher-cost dedicated/private unless primary tier shows sustained degradation or request-level override present
When primary model instance is unavailable, automatic variant escape occurs to a compatible quantized variant with documented quality delta and telemetry annotation
Unit and integration tests cover latency delta detection, net-penalty computation, and fallback variant resolution logic
Observability: dashboards show decision distribution, false-positive demotions, and rollback counts over last 7d
technical_design: Signal inputs: rolling p50 and p95 windows (default 1m/5m), recent packet loss and TCP retransmit rate from edge telemetry, and region capacity headroom metrics
Score formulation: base_score = alpha * normalized_p50 + beta * normalized_p95 + gamma * net_penalty where alpha + beta + gamma = 1. Default beta (p95 weight) = 0.6 to bias tail latency sensitivity

Net_penalty: composite 0..1 penalty computed from packet_loss, retransmit_rate, and inter-pop RTT jitter; penalty is applied multiplicatively to increase final_score (worse is higher score). The penalty uses clipped exponentiation to avoid linear amplification from noisy signals

Latency deltas: compute delta against global median and region historical baseline. Use smoothed exponential decay to avoid reacting to single outliers. A sustained p95 delta threshold (configurable) toggles a demotion flag
Hysteresis and lockouts: implement two-tier lock: soft lock (60s) prevents immediate re-promotion; hard lock (5m) required to fully re-evaluate after manual override or emergency fallback

Tier routing constraints: maintain route affinity arrays per customer that encode allowed tiers and cost budgets. Arbitrator will only select a higher tier if the lower tier's final_score exceeds configured threshold and predicted cost delta is within budget

Variant fallback: variant catalog service maps primary model -> compatible variants with expected quality delta. Fallback policy picks the lowest-cost compatible variant that satisfies availability and runtime compatibility; annotate requests with variant_reason
API surface: REST endpoint for decision simulation (/internal/routing/simulate) and streaming debug for sampled requests to help SREs replay decisions
Storage: short-lived decisions (30 days) in time-series store for dashboards; archived decisions in S3 for incident forensics
implementation_todos: Add p50/p95 windowed aggregates to telemetry ingestion path (update collector config)
Create net_penalty calculation library and unit tests
Implement arbitrator service with decision API and simulation endpoint
Integrate variant-catalog lookup and annotate chosen variant reasoning
Add decision logs to existing tracing and routing dashboards
Write e2e tests with synthetic latency spike scenarios
Prepare rollout plan and feature flag for gradual enablement
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable on 5% of internal traffic in us-west-2 for 48h. Monitor p95, 5xx, and cross-region egress costs.
Phase 2: expand to 25% of production for low-risk tenants, monitor for oscillation and false demotions for 72h
Phase 3: region-wide rollout with 60s soft lock and 5m hard lock. Allow immediate rollback to legacy selector via global flag
Fallback test: simulate primary model unavailability and assert variant escape chosen and annotated
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboard: Routing > Arbitrator Decisions: decision_rate, demotion_rate, avg_final_score by region
Alert: demotion_rate > 3x baseline for 15m => P1 paging to SRE
Alert: oscillation_detector triggers if region swaps > 5 in 10m => investigate hysteresis tuning
SLO guardrail: increased p95 for affected customers should not exceed 10% above baseline for >30m
Logs: sampled per-request decision trace persisted to trace store with correlation_id
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-weighting p95 could send excess traffic cross-region increasing egress costs. Mitigation: cost budget check before promoting higher-cost tier and trial on internal traffic first.
Risk: Noisy network signals produce false penalties. Mitigation: use clipped exponent and require persistence window before demotion.
Risk: Variant fallback quality regression. Mitigation: require that variant catalog has historical eval score; include quick rollback label and rate-limit variant escapes per customer.
Risk: Selector complexity increases debugging time. Mitigation: structured decision logs and simulation endpoint for replay
